Finding submitted.

**Deviation — MFN obligation burdening Customer (§ 7.2, p0026)**

Section 7.2 requires *Customer* to "disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives" before engaging another provider. The MFN runs against us, not in our favour: it is unlimited as to product, duration, and comparability, with no reasonable-comparison carve-outs, so it fails the fallback (defined product / 12 months / carve-outs) and lands in walk-away territory as an open-ended duty to extend Vendor any better third-party terms. It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

Redline (validated, ok:true): delete p0026 in full — the smallest edit reaching the preferred position, leaving any Vendor-granted MFN intact. Kept separate from the EXCLUSIVITY analysis (§ 12.4 non-solicit / non-compete) to avoid double-flagging the same term.
